scope: Explicit recovery of the insertion and alignment OCS points of exact DRW_Text after exactly one actual legacy extrusion application by a DXF reader or caller. DXF output only; no default behavior or class layout change. Derived ATTRIB, ATTDEF and MTEXT are excluded.

authority.oda: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1 §20.4.3 defines TEXT insertion, alignment, extrusion, elevation and alignment flags.
authority.finding: DXF TEXT insertion and alignment are OCS points; the latter participates when horizontal or vertical alignment is nonzero.

physical.method: Two R2010 TEXT entities authored from scratch using ezdxf 1.4.5 with tilted (0,1,0) and negative-Z (0,0,-1) normals, separate insertion/alignment, middle-center alignment, 25-degree rotation and nonzero thickness/width/oblique. ODA File Converter 27.1.0 saved AC1024 DWG and a DXF readback. Native DWG reader selected both TEXT records and wrote a native OCS DXF, which was then read with DXF applyExt=true and re-emitted both with and without explicit inverse recovery. These are selected records, not full-document conversion. Scratch-only inputs; no drawing fixture is committed.

observation: For the tilted TEXT, ODA and selected native DXF agree OCS insertion (1,2,3) and alignment (3,4,3), WCS (-1,3,2) and (-3,3,4). DXF applyExt=true followed by the ordinary writer reinterprets transformed WCS points as OCS and moves both. The negative-Z case similarly misplaces both anchors. Explicit inverse recovery restores them; ezdxf independently confirms both OCS and WCS points, extrusion, height, rotation, oblique, width, thickness and both alignment flags match ODA for both records.
important_dwg_boundary: The current DWG TEXT dispatch appends native OCS data without applying extrusion. Its applyExt=true and false observations were identical; this receipt does not claim a DWG-reader extrusion bug and the helper must not be used on that native state as though a transform had occurred.
implementation: An explicit exact-DRW_Text free-function overload validates finite points, normal and key geometry, nonzero normal and finite inverse projections; it copies before publication, preserves all metadata, supports input/output aliasing and leaves output unchanged on failure. Exact runtime type and TEXT tag reject derived objects and type spoofing. Existing consumers and unopted writer paths are unchanged.

validation.focused: ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R ^libdxfrw_dxf_legacy_extrusion$ --output-on-failure: 1/1 passed. ASCII/Binary DXF roundtrip with four normals checks both anchors, alignments and metadata. Controls include no-extrusion no-op, nonunit normal, invalid/overflow projection and output/alias preservation, ATTRIB/ATTDEF/MTEXT derived input/output refusal, type spoofing, destination preservation and same-writer retry. Prior CIRCLE/ARC and SOLID/TRACE cases run in the same test.
validation.independent: ezdxf 1.4.5 compared ODA readback and corrected selected DXF for both normals, both OCS/WCS anchors, normal, height, rotation, width, oblique, thickness, horizontal and vertical alignment; all matched.

limits: The caller must know an actual transform was applied exactly once and the object has not since been edited in a way that invalidates its frame; the helper cannot infer this.
The physical source covers two normals and selected DXF records only, not full document conversion, native font rendering or all alignment profiles.
DWG emission using this helper output is not qualified. Scratch artifacts are ephemeral and no DWG/DXF fixture is committed.
